question: Should OpenClaw accept this experiment-gated core Claw update-planning and capability-consent contract as the next slice of the open lifecycle stack after its parent diagnostics work lands?
rationale: This PR creates a new CLI and persisted-plan/consent boundary; correctness alone cannot decide whether that product model belongs in core or how its stacked slices should be sequenced.

options.title: Sponsor the staged core contract
options.body: Confirm the read-only planner as the intended next core slice, conditional on parent-stack landing and inspectable redaction proof.

options.title: Keep the capability external
options.body: Pause this core contract and direct the grouped update workflow toward a plugin or ClawHub-owned implementation if core lifecycle ownership is not intended.

options.title: Narrow before adoption
options.body: Request a reduced diagnostic-only surface until the broader apply and consent model has explicit owner approval.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the staged core contract
recommendation.body: Confirm the read-only planner as the intended next core slice, conditional on parent-stack landing and inspectable redaction proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is assigned and authored the substantive review requirements for the planner's ownership and update semantics.
